name: Alphonse
bio: A young man of Wilde's Paris circle in December 1898, described to Reginald Turner as 'your little friend Alphonse'. He was arrested one night for blackmail after demanding fifteen francs, being given ten and a cab-fare, and making a scene on being put out of the house. Wilde's verdict: 'quite an imp, though attractive in love-scenes'.
bio_note: Added 2026-08-06, from the General Index entry 'Alphonse (boy), 1107'. **HE IS NOT ALPHONSE CONWAY.** The map's other Alphonse is [[conway]], the Worthing boy of the summer of 1894 who appears in the 1895 plea of justification. This one is Paris, December 1898, is Turner's friend rather than Wilde's, and is a different person; the editors index them separately. The near-collision is exactly why the index is worth reading - a name-match against the map would have silently folded him into Conway. HE SURVIVES UNDER A FIRST NAME ONLY. No age is given and none is inferred. WHAT THE RECORD SAYS PLAINLY is that he extorted money and was arrested for it; that is kept rather than softened, and so is Wilde's amused tone about it, which tells you as much about Wilde as about Alphonse. THE FOLIO IS A CENSUS OF THE PARIS EXILE HOUSEHOLD in December 1898 and should be read as one: Sir John Ashton and his 'little friend' Joseph (both already on this map, connected on this same page), Turner's 'little friend' Alphonse, and Hylton with 'his boy' Herbert. Four young men in three sentences, all described to Wilde's closest correspondent in the same possessive formula. DUPLICATE REMOVED 2026-08-06, per Lovelle: this node first carried the letter TWICE - once on a context engagement with Wilde and again on the connection to Turner. The engagement was wrong on both counts. It printed the same paragraph twice on his panel, and it implied a Wilde-Alphonse pairing that the source does not make: the letter is Wilde writing TO Turner ABOUT Turner's friend. Wilde is the witness here, not a party. The evidence now lives once, on [[turner]]'s connection, where it belongs.
